title: "Styling"

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

`quartifyr_styling` (the Python engine bundled at `inst/python/`) is
code-first generation of the docx `reference-doc` used when rendering a
quartifyr shell with Quarto, the abbreviations YAML →
`abbreviations.tex` bridge consumed by `quarto-plus`, and headless Word
field/cross-reference post-processing via LibreOffice. Called from R via
a `pyro` bridge (the `styling_*()` functions below), or standalone via
the `quartifyr-styling` CLI:

```bash
uv venv .venv --python 3.12   # from a checkout of the repo
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e '.[dev]'
```

## What a style YAML can do

Every option below is a YAML diff from the default preset -- fonts,
color, all-caps headings, shaded/padded code blocks, banded tables, all
changed together here to show the range in one comparison. Both are the
*same* `examples/demo-report/report.qmd` content, rendered through the
same pipeline, differing only in which reference-doc was built from
which style YAML:

<div style="display:flex; gap:12px; flex-wrap:wrap;">
<div><img src="../man/figures/style-gallery-default.png" alt="Default style: black serif Times New Roman heading and body text, plain gray code block background, no padding" width="440" loading="lazy"><p style="text-align:center; font-size:0.85em;">default.yaml, untouched</p></div>
<div><img src="../man/figures/style-gallery-branded.png" alt="Branded style: blue all-caps sans-serif Calibri heading, Calibri body text, warm yellow code block background with visible padding" width="440" loading="lazy"><p style="text-align:center; font-size:0.85em;">a ~15-line override</p></div>
</div>

```yaml
fonts:
  body: "Calibri"
  heading: "Calibri"
  monospace: "Consolas"
colors:
  heading: "#0054AD"
  title: "#0054AD"
  table_header_fill: "#CFE2FF"
  rule: "#0054AD"
heading:
  all_caps: true
code:
  background_color: "#FFF3CD"
  padding_pt: 4
table:
  banding: true
```

```r
quartifyr::styling_build_reference_docx(
  style = "inst/python/styles/default.yaml",
  override = "acme-branding.yaml",
  out = "acme-reference.docx"
)
```

See "Style YAML reference" below for every option this can touch, and
"Pulling and editing a project's own style YAML" for a lower-friction
way to build an override like the one above than hand-writing it from
scratch.

## Style YAML reference

Every top-level section below is a dataclass in
`inst/python/quartifyr_styling/schema.py`, validated against
`inst/python/styles/schema.json` (point an editor at it via
`# yaml-language-server: $schema=...` for autocomplete). `override` YAMLs
(`build`'s `--override`, most `styling_*()` functions' `override`
argument) only need the keys that differ -- deep-merged onto `style` at
load time, not a second full copy.

### `fonts`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | Body text font family | `"Times New Roman"` |
| `heading` | Title/subtitle/heading font family | `"Times New Roman"` |
| `monospace` | Code block/inline code font family | `"Courier New"` |
| `sizes.body` | Body text size (pt) | `11` |
| `sizes.title` | Title page title size (pt) | `26` |
| `sizes.subtitle` | Title page subtitle size (pt) | `16` |
| `sizes.heading.1`-`6` | Per-level heading size (pt) -- a level deeper than any key here falls back to the smallest defined | `16, 14, 12, 11, 11, 11` |
| `sizes.caption` | Figure/table caption size (pt) | `10` |
| `sizes.footnote` | Footer/footnote text size (pt) | `9` |
| `sizes.toc` | Table of contents entry size (pt) | `11` |

### `colors`

Every value is a `"#RRGGBB"` hex color.

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | Body text | `#000000` |
| `heading` | Heading text | `#000000` |
| `title` | Title/subtitle text | `#000000` |
| `caption` | Figure/table caption text | `#000000` |
| `table_header_fill` | Table header row background | `#D9D9D9` |
| `table_border` | Table border lines | `#000000` |
| `rule` | Rule under the title (if shown) | `#000000` |

### `page`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `"letter"` or `"a4"` | `"letter"` |
| `margins_in.top`/`bottom`/`left`/`right` | Page margins (inches) | `1` each |

### `paragraph`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `line_spacing` | Body text line spacing multiplier | `1.15` |
| `space_after_pt` | Space after a body paragraph (pt) | `8` |
| `alignment` | `"left"`/`"justify"`/`"center"`/`"right"` | `"left"` |

### `heading`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bold` | Bold heading text | `true` |
| `space_before_pt`/`space_after_pt` | Spacing around a heading (pt) | `12`/`6` |
| `keep_with_next` | Keep a heading on the same page as the paragraph after it | `true` |
| `all_caps` | All-caps *visual* transform (OOXML `w:caps`) -- the underlying text is untouched | `false` |

### `table`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `style` | Word table style name | `"Table Grid"` |
| `header_bold` | Bold the header row | `true` |
| `banding` | Alternating row shading | `false` |

### `synopsis`

Governs the synopsis section's definition-list look (bold label line,
indented value beneath it) -- see `synopsis-style:` in the [Quarto
extension](quarto-extension.html) article for the three layouts this
applies to.

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label_space_before_pt`/`label_space_after_pt` | Spacing around a label line (pt) | `12`/`2` |
| `value_space_after_pt` | Space after a value line (pt) | `2` |
| `value_indent_in` | Value line indent (inches) | `0.25` |
| `alignment` | Overrides `paragraph.alignment` for values only; omit to inherit it | unset |

### `title_page`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `show_rule_under_title` | Rule under the title (color from `colors.rule`) | `true` |
| `fields` | Which title-page fields appear, in order (a list, not a map -- pandoc's Lua metadata tables don't preserve map key order) | `report_type, title, subtitle, date, lead_scientist, version, confidentiality` |

### `footer`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `show_page_number` | Show the page-number field | `true` |
| `text` | Optional static footer text | `""` |

### `code`

Styles fenced code blocks/inline code (pandoc's own `Source Code`/
`Verbatim Char` docx styles). Defaults match pandoc's own built-in
fallback, so leaving this section untouched doesn't change existing
rendered output.

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font_size` | Code text size (pt) -- family comes from `fonts.monospace` above | `10` |
| `background_color` | Shaded background | `#F1F3F5` |
| `padding_pt` | Space before/after the shaded block (vertical only -- OOXML paragraph shading has no horizontal-padding concept) | `0` |

### `equation`

| Key | Controls | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font` | Docx-wide default math font (applied post-render by `apply-layout`, not `build` -- pandoc's docx writer doesn't carry this setting through from the reference-doc template). Font family only; an unstyled equation inherits its size from the surrounding paragraph | `"Cambria Math"` |

## `build`: style YAML → reference-doc

```r
quartifyr::styling_build_reference_docx(
  style = "inst/python/styles/default.yaml",
  out = "org-reference.docx"
)
```

```bash
quartifyr-styling build \
  --style inst/python/styles/default.yaml \
  --out org-reference.docx
```

<img src="../man/figures/styling-build.gif" alt="Terminal recording of quartifyr-styling build generating a docx reference-doc from a style YAML file" width="700" loading="lazy">

Add `override`/`--override` with just the keys that differ from the
default preset (fonts, colors, page setup, ...) to brand a new
organization; see `inst/python/styles/default.yaml` for the full schema
and `inst/python/quartifyr_styling/schema.py` for validation rules (hex
colors, positive sizes, valid page sizes, ...).

`style`/`override`/`out` are plain file paths, not fixed locations. An
org can keep its style YAML anywhere, and most project authors never
need to run `build` at all: reuse an already-built `.docx`, distributed
however your org already shares binary artifacts.

The generated reference-doc also sets `<w:updateFields w:val="true"/>`
in `word/settings.xml`, so real Word automatically recalculates every
field (ToC, `SEQ`, `REF`, `PAGE`, ...) the moment a delivered document is
opened; no manual "select all, F9", no LibreOffice involved for that
case.

## `abbrevs`: footnotes YAML → abbreviations bridge

```r
quartifyr::styling_build_abbreviations_tex(
  footnotes = "report/standard_footnotes.yaml",
  out = "report/shell/abbreviations.tex"
)
```

Converts a project's `standard_footnotes.yaml` (`reportifyr`'s own
format) into the `abbreviations.tex` that `quarto-plus` reads to render
a "only abbreviations actually used via `\gls{}`" list.

## `apply-layout`: header/footer + page-number split

```r
quartifyr::styling_apply_layout(
  docx = "report/shell/report.docx",
  qmd = "report.qmd",
  status = "draft"
)
```

Run on the shell docx right after the Quarto render, before
`reportifyr`'s pass-2 fill. Reads the `.qmd`'s frontmatter for
`header-format:` and applies it to a two-zone page header (template flush
left, draft/final status flush right). Also reads `confidentiality:` for
the footer's left zone, and, if the `.qmd` uses `{{< body-start >}}`,
splits the rendered docx into title-page/front-matter/body OOXML
sections so the whole front matter numbers in lowercase roman (starting
at "i") and the body restarts at arabic "1". A `.qmd` with neither
`header-format:` nor `{{< body-start >}}` is left untouched; both are
opt-in.

Also reads `crossref-hyperlinks:` (default `true`); `false` strips the
`\h` hyperlink switch from every figure/table/appendix cross-reference's
`REF` field, document-wide. `"same-page"` can't be resolved here (no
real pagination exists yet on the pass-1 shell); it just marks each
crossref for the next command.

## `resolve-same-page-crossrefs`: post-fill crossref resolution

```r
quartifyr::styling_resolve_same_page_crossrefs("report/draft/report-draft.docx")
```

Resolves the markers `apply-layout`'s `crossref-hyperlinks: "same-page"`
left behind, now that `reportifyr`'s pass 2 has filled in real content
and pagination means something; run on the *filled* draft/final docx,
not the shell. A no-op (skips LibreOffice entirely) if the document has
no same-page markers. Read-only with respect to LibreOffice: it drives a
headless-LibreOffice macro only to read page numbers, never to re-save
the docx.

**Experimental.** Inherits the same intermittent-hang behavior
documented for `recalculate-fields` below. Off by default in
`render_report()`.

## `recalculate-fields`: headless ToC/field recalculation

```r
quartifyr::styling_recalculate_fields("path/to/report-final.docx")
```

Drives headless LibreOffice to recalculate a docx's Word ToC (page
numbers, entries) in place; for non-interactive pipelines that never
open the file in an application at all. Real Word already recalculates
fields automatically on open (via the reference-doc's own
`updateFields` setting above), so this is only needed for headless
consumers.

**Experimental and known-flaky.** Real-world runs against the same
document have produced three different outcomes: it hangs, it exits
cleanly as a silent no-op, or it actually succeeds. Reproduced both
sandboxed and in a plain native terminal, ruling out sandboxing as the
cause. Off by default (`render_report(..., recalculate_fields = FALSE)`).
When it does fail, it only produces a warning, not a render failure;
the document is still fully usable, just needs a manual "select all,
F9" in Word.

## Pulling and editing a project's own style YAML

```r
# Copy the bundled default template/style into a project
quartifyr::styling_example_template(dir = "templates")
style <- quartifyr::styling_example_style(dir = ".")

# Edit in place ...
style$heading$all_caps <- TRUE
style$colors$heading <- "#0054AD"

# ... and save back out as just the diff from the default
quartifyr::styling_save_overrides(style, file = "overrides.yaml")
```

```yaml
# overrides.yaml
heading:
  all_caps: true
colors:
  heading: "#0054AD"
```

That override YAML is what `style`/`override` (or `--style`/`--override`)
take everywhere else in this article -- `styling_build_reference_docx()`
deep-merges it onto the base at load time, so it's a diff to keep in a
project, not a second full style YAML to maintain by hand.

For a narrower, one-off edit to an *existing* style YAML (not
necessarily one just pulled via `styling_example_style()`):

```r
quartifyr::styling_update_style(
  list(code = list(background_color = "#FFF3CD")),
  file = "overrides.yaml",
  yes = TRUE
)
```

Deep-merges the update onto `file`'s content, in place -- a
`modifyList()`-style edit without hand-copying the rest of the file.
`yes = TRUE` is required: this rewrites the whole file, so any comments
it had are lost.
